captureNotice: Screenshots of real application components using sample data. Colors, permissions and available options may differ with your configuration.
tasksCaption: Task manager: switch views on the left; plan, create tasks and open settings on the right.
lifecycleCaption: The lifecycle shows the current stage. This ribbon is informational: use Change status to perform a transition.
generalStep1: Click the + next to Projects, enter a name, then open the new project.
generalStep2: Add the people you need, then configure local folders and external connections in Locations and connections. Check the active working directory before starting an agent.
generalStep3: Use the project’s + to add a conversation or manager. Start with a specific task and review the result before retaining it.
generalEffect1: Creates a new project, not a task inside an existing project.
generalEffect2: Adds a conversation or resource to the selected project. A project can have several task managers, but only one deliverables manager and one automations manager.
generalEffect3: Opens project administration: information, people, journal, agents, locations and connections. Available screens depend on your permissions.
conversationsStep1: Open a Codex conversation to work with tools, or a simple chat to exchange messages without tool execution.
conversationsStep2: Describe the expected outcome, files and constraints. Check the model, reasoning effort and permissions below the message field.
conversationsStep3: Read each proposed action before approving it. Review changes and documents afterwards: an agent’s answer does not replace human validation.
conversationsEffect1: Send starts a turn. Stop interrupts ongoing work; it does not undo changes already made.
conversationsEffect2: No details hides routine technical activity; Collapsed details keeps it available; Show all expands it. Alerts and decision requests remain visible. This does not change permissions.
conversationsEffect3: Chooses the engine and work permissions. Verbosity controls answer detail, effort controls reasoning work, and summary controls the model’s provided reasoning summary.
tasksStep1: Choose New task, enter a title, then set the owner, priority, dates and validation criteria before saving.
tasksStep2: Use Board for cards, Planning for dates and dependencies, Advice for analysis and Journal for changes. Click a task to open its detail page; use Back to return to the list.
tasksStep3: AI planning first proposes main tasks. Review the proposal before applying it; break a task into subtasks afterwards if needed.
tasksEffect1: Opens a task form, then saves its fields. Not every form change is saved automatically.
tasksButton2: Plan with AI / Break down with AI
tasksEffect2: Planning proposes a plan or a reschedule; breakdown proposes subtasks for one task. Review the proposal before applying it.
tasksButton3: Run with an agent / Validate and complete
tasksEffect3: Execution applies to an agent-configured subtask. Review its output before completing it. Blocking dependencies can prevent it from starting.
deliverablesStep1: Create a deliverable and describe its expected outcome and criteria. Link its main task to manage the owner and due date.
deliverablesStep2: In Documents, choose Add a document, select files and optionally enter a comment. Every document has its own version numbers.
deliverablesStep3: Use Change status to start constitution and finalize. If validation is required, review the frozen snapshot in Validation before deciding. History retains events; reopening resumes work.
deliverablesEffect1: Adding records a document. Its menu offers available actions such as preview, versions, download or removal. Restoring an older version creates a new version rather than rewriting history.
deliverablesEffect2: Shows allowed transitions only. Finalizing freezes a snapshot; it does not mean a human has approved it. Validation is requested only when required.
deliverablesEffect3: Links agent work to the deliverable. Retained documents go through a draft and versioned recording; code and temporary files are not published documents.
automationsStep1: Add the automations manager to the project, then create an automation with an explicit instruction and schedule.
automationsStep2: Check scope, permissions and timing before activation. An automation may face the same approval requests as manual work.
automationsStep3: Review runs and their results. Diagnose a failed run; failure does not prove that earlier actions were undone.
automationsEffect1: Controls future scheduled runs. Pausing does not delete the configuration or history.
automationsEffect2: Distinguishes expected triggers, ongoing work and final results. Review errors and output before retrying.
automationsEffect3: Saves instructions and scheduling. Check the frequency to avoid unwanted work or costs.
projectAdministrationStep1: Open the project, then People to manage participants and groups. Check access before sharing a confidential deliverable.
projectAdministrationStep2: In Locations and connections, distinguish the managed local space, attached local folders, and Git, SSH/SFTP or FTP/FTPS connections. Internal .mergeron data is hidden by default in the project file listing. Browsing a location does not change the agent’s active working directory.
projectAdministrationStep3: In Agent management, configure shared knowledge and integrations. Selecting a connector and authenticating it are separate operations; verify effective permissions too.
projectAdministrationEffect1: Changes the conversation’s working folder. Folder aliases are display names only; operations still use the real server path.
projectAdministrationEffect2: Saves the project selection. It does not create external accounts or automatically connect services. An unchecked option is not proof of isolation without verifying effective access.
projectAdministrationEffect3: Adds a reviewed proposal to shared knowledge. An agent suggestion alone does not change approved memory.
administrationStep1: Limit administration to authorized people. In Codex, Account is the first tab: connect an account to enable the others.
administrationStep2: Server contains Current version, Update, Backup and Socket. Infrastructure shows the Manager and service health; these are not project settings.
administrationStep3: Start troubleshooting with Logs or Diagnostics. Global files and Terminal affect the whole server: check the path and impact before commands or deletion.
administrationEffect1: Refresh searches for an image without installing it. Update checks prerequisites and asks for confirmation before installation. Follow progress during temporary server unavailability.
administrationEffect2: Configure retention in Logs. After saving, archives beyond the age or count limits may be deleted automatically; the active file stays protected.
administrationButton3: Restore previous version / delete a backup
administrationEffect3: Restoration returns to the saved state according to Manager progress. Deleting a backup is permanent and removes that rollback option; check its usefulness before treating it as routine cleanup.
